messages:
ben_support: Customer (Acme) opened an escalated ticket — after migrating services to a new AWS account + VPC peering, their service clients started failing discovery. They get NXDOMAIN for SRV records like _grpc._tcp.internal-svc.acme.local. Repro steps from customer: curl to control-plane ok, service resolution via client fails. Can we triage?

sam_sre: Can you paste a dig/nslookup from inside their app subnet? also need VPC ID & account id.

ben_support: Pasting the dig output they provided (from an app pod):

```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> _grpc._tcp.internal-svc.acme.local SRV +short
;; global options: +cmd
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
;; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```

ben_support: They also ran `kubectl exec` to a busybox pod and saw NXDOMAIN from the node resolver. VPC id vpc-0a1b2c3d account 123456789012.

priya_support: Quick checklist: 1) Is there a Route53 private hosted zone for acme.local? 2) Is that hosted zone associated with the new VPC? 3) Any overlapping private zones or resolver rules in a shared account? 4) Firewall/NACL?

dima_net: +1 on hosted zone assoc. In our past incidents a leftover private hosted zone in the original account (or a resolver rule in a shared account) returned NXDOMAIN to the peered VPC. Need to check: hosted zone IDs and VPC associations across accounts.

ben_support: Checked customer console (they gave read-only link). It looks like they have two private hosted zones: zOLD (acme.local) in account A (old-account) and zNEW in account B (new-account), but zNEW is NOT associated to the new VPC. zOLD is associated to the old VPC only. They said they deleted the old VPC but left the hosted zone.

infra-bot: route53-change: resolver-rule-updated by ops@redwood — 2101239900 — reference: https://internal.redwood/changes/CR-9876

sam_sre: If zNEW isn't associated with the VPC, the resolver will consult other rules or return NXDOMAIN. Also check cross-account resolver rules (Outbound/ConditionalForwarder) in the shared DNS account — priority can shadow local records.

ben_support: Customer attached `dig +trace` and aws cli checks. They see a conditional-resolver rule in the shared DNS account pointing acme.local -> outbound to 10.1.2.3 (old resolver). That resolver is now returning NXDOMAIN for SRV.

priya_support: Workaround while we fix assoc: add a temporary CNAME/SRV in the shared resolver's target to point to the correct service, or update the resolver rule priority so the VPC-local hosted zone wins. But long term we should associate zNEW to the new VPC.

dima_net: I'll open a change to associate hosted zone z-0abcde12345 to vpc-0a1b2c3d in account 123456789012. Planning window: 15m. Also will update the conditional forwarder rule to prefer local resolution if present.

ben_support: Customer asked for repro commands. Sent these: 
```
# from a node in the affected VPC
dig _grpc._tcp.internal-svc.acme.local SRV @169.254.169.253
# check hosted zone associations
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "acme.local" --query "HostedZones[*].Id"
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/z-0abcde12345
```

sam_sre: Also verify resolver rule assoc: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-endpoint-outbound` and `list-resolver-rules` in the shared-dns account — sometimes rule priority is accidentally set to 0.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: change CR-10321 created to associate hosted zone and update resolver priority. MR: https://internal.redwood/changes/CR-10321 

(prior to change) ben_support: customer is nervous about downtime — they want rollback steps. We suggested: 1) dissociate if rollback needed, 2) re-add old association temporarily, 3) revert resolver rule priority.

dima_net: Change executed — associated z-0abcde12345 -> vpc-0a1b2c3d @ 2101242000, bumped resolver rule priority in shared account to prefer VPC local.

ben_support: After assoc — customer ran dig from pod and shared output: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> _grpc._tcp.internal-svc.acme.local SRV +short
0 5 8080 svc-12.acme.local.
```

priya_support: Verified SRV returned, client now does discovery and connects. Customer confirmed their app instances are healthy. :tada:

dima_net: Leaving a note in internal runbook: when migrating accounts, ensure new private hosted zone is associated to all target VPCs and check for conditional resolver rules in shared-dns account that may shadow local zones.

sam_sre: Marking incident as resolved pending post-mortem. Assigning action items: owner=dima_net (assoc hosted zone + update runbook), owner=priya_support (customer follow-up & add example commands to KB).

ben_support: Closing loop with customer and updating ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
